title: Apple's New iPhone Lineup Includes First Foldable Model
paragraphs: Apple has unveiled its first foldable iPhone, called the iPhone Duo, as part of its latest lineup of smartphones.

The phone was announced on September 9, 2026, at Apple's annual iPhone event, where the company also introduced the iPhone 18 Pro and two new smartwatches. The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999, which makes it far more expensive than the iPhone 18 Pro, which starts at $1,199. Pre-orders began on October 16 in more than 70 countries, and the phone went on sale on October 23.

When it is closed, the iPhone Duo has a 5.4-inch outer screen. When it is opened, it reveals a 7.6-inch inner screen, which Apple says is 50% larger than the screen of the iPhone 18 Pro Max. The phone uses the same A20 Pro chip as the iPhone 18 Pro, and it is made of titanium. Unlike most recent iPhones, it does not have Face ID. Instead, users unlock it with a fingerprint sensor in the side button. It also has no slot for a physical SIM card. It is available in two colors, star white and night sky.
Apple's new CEO, John Ternus, described the iPhone Duo as the most transformational change to the iPhone since the original model.

Foldable phones have been available from other companies, such as Samsung, for several years. Interestingly, Apple priced its phone $100 below Samsung's latest foldable model, the Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra. Before the launch, the research company IDC had expected the iPhone Duo to cost about $2,500. Nabila Popal of IDC described its target customers as a very elite group of consumers.
However, some features will not be available everywhere at first. For example, Apple's new AI version of Siri will not initially be available in the European Union.
